messages:
jordan: Heads-up — support ticket from Acme (Dedicated) reporting intermittent KMS decrypt failures during peak (about 5% of requests). They see AccessDeniedException and sometimes InvalidCiphertextException. Happening for traffic routed through cross-account role (acct-b). They're in prod, saw spike around an alias rotation window. Need quick triage.

mira: Can you paste a sample failing log (CloudTrail request ID + error)? Also which key arn/alias and approximate window?

jordan: Paste from customer logs (sanitized): 
```
{ "eventTime":"2026-03-05T18:12:34Z", "eventName":"Decrypt", "errorCode":"AccessDeniedException", "errorMessage":"User: arn:aws:sts::111111111111:assumed-role/infra-cross-account/role-session is not authorized to perform: kms:Decrypt on resource: arn:aws:kms:us-east-1:222222222222:key/abcd-ef01-... with encryptionContext mismatch", "requestID":"c4f7a2d3-1111-2222-3333-444455556666" }
```
Alias: arn:aws:kms:us-east-1:222222222222:alias/acme-prod-primary; rotation was at ~18:10UTC (alias swapped).

ashok: Two quick suspects: 1) encryptionContext condition in key policy/grant causing mismatch for some sessions, 2) ephemeral STS session policy or session tags not carrying required context so grant condition fails. Also alias swap can cause a brief period where requests referencing key id vs alias mismatch behavior depending on client caching.

samir: Do we know if the customer's SDKs are using keyId (uuid) or alias? If they cache key metadata, they might send ciphertext that references the previous key id while alias now points to a new key — that shouldn't cause AccessDenied usually, but if they rely on a grant bound to the previous key id it could.

mira: Jordan — can you ask for a failing base64 ciphertext header (first bytes) or the ciphertextBlob's KeyId returned in response to Encrypt call? Also ask for CloudTrail event where Encrypt happened -> that will show keyId used.

jordan: Asked the customer for encrypt-side CloudTrail. They sent an Encrypt event earlier: keyId: arn:aws:kms:us-east-1:222222222222:key/ff12-... at 18:08:12Z. Then alias swap at 18:10. So some decrypts reference old key id.

ashok: Ok that matches a rotation race: encrypt -> old key id, alias swapped to new key, decrypts later routed with role from acct-b that only has a grant on new key (or a key policy referencing alias). Grants are per-key, not alias. If cross-account grant was created after rotation, old key won't have it. That leads to AccessDenied.

mira: Two remediation options: 1) re-create grant on the previous key for cross-account role (temporary), or 2) ensure customers re-encrypt with new key (bulk rewrap), or 3) update IAM/Key policy to allow decrypts for both key ids during rotation windows.

samir: Also check encryptionContext: customer uses encryptionContext {"client":"acme-web","purpose":"session"}. If key policy has a condition kms:EncryptionContext:client then sessions without that exact key will fail with AccessDenied even if grant exists. Need to verify the failing events include encryptionContext in the request and that the values match exactly (string case/whitespace).

jordan: Customer pasted failing Decrypt event and it shows encryptionContext: null for ~20% of failing calls (their CDN edge worker strips header). So two factors: missing encryptionContext + key id/grant mismatch.

ashok: That explains InvalidCiphertextException maybe — if ciphertext was truncated by CDN. But AccessDenied is from policy/grant mismatch. Action: add a temporary grant on old key for role arn:aws:iam::111111111111:role/infra-cross-account OR update key policy to permit decrypt from that role for both keys. After that, advise customer to re-encrypt tokens or ensure edge preserves encryptionContext header.

mira: Jordan, can you run these checks (or ask customer) and capture CloudTrail event IDs for one failing Decrypt and one successful Decrypt from same token? Also confirm whether they call KMS directly or via our proxy (Redwood private)? If via our proxy, ensure proxy forwards encryptionContext and doesn't cache stale key metadata.

jordan: They call KMS directly from their infra (not through us). Sent two request IDs: failing c4f7a2d3-..., successful b9e1a7c0-... I advised temp grant on old key and to patch edge worker. They're going to try creating grant now.

samir: For grant creation CLI (if needed):
```
aws kms create-grant --key-id 1234abcd-ff12-... --grantee-principal arn:aws:iam::111111111111:role/infra-cross-account --operations Decrypt --name "temp-cross-account-decrypt"
```
Note: grants expire on key deletion only; consider revoke after stable. If key policy has encryptionContext condition, grants won't bypass that — need grantConstraints if applicable.

mira: Also check STS: if they assume-role and pass session tags, and key policy expects kms:EncryptionContext:client from session tag, ensure tags are present and not stripped. Example assume role call:
```
aws sts assume-role --role-arn arn:aws:iam::111111111111:role/infra-cross-account --role-session-name web-123 --duration-seconds 3600 --serial-number ... --token-code ...
```
Session policy example that can break things: `{"Version":"2012-10-17","Statement":[{"Effect":"Allow","Action":"kms:Decrypt","Resource":"*","Condition":{"StringEquals":{"kms:EncryptionContext:client":"acme-web"}}}]}`

jordan: Customer created the grant on old key; they reported immediate reduction in errors from 5% -> ~0.2%. They will patch edge to forward encryptionContext and plan a bulk rewrap during low traffic.

ashok: Good. Follow-up: document best-practice rotation flow in KB: steps to rotate without cross-account disruption: 1) create new key, 2) copy grants/policy to new key, 3) do rolling re-encrypt or dual-read support, 4) after grace period, revoke grants on old key, 5) schedule alias swap or swap alias only after clients updated.

mira: I'll open a short KB PR and link this thread + CloudTrail snippets (sanitized). Jordan, please paste final customer confirmation and mark ticket as 'escalation resolved' when they confirm after rewrap. :thumbsup:

security-bot: incident-note: escalation-1801234567 closed by jordan at 2026-03-06T03:12:00Z

jordan: Will do — customer confirmed. Thanks all :+1:
